analysis.title: Rates Spark: Leaning hawkish, but no action
key_insights: The Fed statement leaned hawkish throughout but did not hike. ING reads this as enough to validate the 10yr UST yield's move back above 5%.

Before the FOMC meeting the 10yr yield had been holding around 4.99%. The initial reaction to the decision was higher, then the yield moved back to 5% and briefly below on Chair Warsh's press conference comments that inflation expectations had been tamed somewhat.

ING argues the Fed still has a job to do to reach the strict 2% price stability Warsh describes. Elevated printed inflation with the Fed on hold is not seen as very protective for the back end, and inflation expectations rose after the decision and Warsh's commentary.
ING maintains its view that the 10yr UST yield is on a journey back toward 5.25%.

The front end took the tone better, with the 2yr yield edging lower. The front end likes the unchanged policy rate and the idea that the Fed is giving the economy time to react to the first 25bp hike. ING sees a world where the Fed is less aggressive in action than in words.
ING expects a steeper curve from both ends, with more of that likely in coming weeks.

The Fed implementation note was broadly unchanged. Implementation rates and mechanisms are unchanged, and MBS principal payments continue to be reinvested into Treasury bills. A plan to shrink the balance sheet, a policy objective for Warsh, is still some way off, with committee recommendations expected closer to the turn of the year. Liquidity is stable and repo is behaving better than a year ago.
The ECB meets Thursday and no rate change is expected. The focus is on wording around a possible December hike, for which markets already discount 23bp of tightening.

Lagarde is expected to face questions on the French bond market turmoil. ING sees the ECB sequence as verbally toning down hawkishness first, then suspending QT and resuming reinvestments, and finally activating the Transmission Protection Instrument. The hurdle for the later steps looks very high.

The debate over raising banks' minimum reserve requirement has taken a back seat. ING thinks it is still too blunt a tool for cutting the ECB's costs, and with excess liquidity closer to levels where larger changes could affect financing conditions, the ECB is unlikely to add volatility.
ING does not expect a major repricing from the ECB meeting. A stronger December hike commitment would nudge a hawkish repricing, but with more than 20bp priced in the reaction should be contained.

Thursday's calendar includes US September PCE (consensus core +0.3% MoM), US Q3 GDP (3.2% annualised expected), eurozone confidence indicators, Italian BTP auctions totalling €7.75bn and a $44bn new 7y US note auction.
